newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia says ZCCM privatisation on track.
newsitem.headline: Zambia says ZCCM privatisation on track.

text.p: The Zambian government said on Tuesday that talks with prospective buyers of the assets of Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) were proceeding as planned and rumours of delays were ill-founded.

"The negotiations are proceeding as scheduled. For example, last week we had discussions with the Kafue consortium in London for a whole week," said co-ordinator of the mining privatisation secretariat of the Zambia Privatisation Agency, Alex Chikwese.
The Kafue consortium comprising Avmin, Noranda, Phelps Dodge and the Commonwealth Development Corp is negotiating for the acquistion of ZCCM's Nkana and Nchanga divisions.
The divisions include five underground mines, one open pit mine, concentrator facilities, a tailing leach plant, a copper smelter and refinery, an acid plant and a cobalt plant.
"We will hold meetings with other bidders until the month end. We are still negotaiting and nothing has stalled," Chikwese told Reuters.
Last month, Gencor Ltd announced it had decided to pull out of a consortium planning to develop the Konkola Deep copper mine, triggering uncertainty about the privatisation process.
Finance Minister Ronald Penza said at the time he believed Zambia remained on track to start selling assets of ZCCM by the end of June.
The government in April invited six bidders for the final negotiations of the sale of ZCCM assets, including Konkola Deep which has been lumped together in one tranche with the Mufulira smelter.
